mainTopic: Dating both destructions of the בית המקדש by the שמיטה and יובל cycles: does the ברייתא follow רבי יהודה or the רבנן?
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier timeline: in נבוכדנצר's second year he conquered יהויקים. The גמרא then returns to a ברייתא that says the second בית המקדש, like the first, was destroyed in מוצאי שביעית. It challenges this with math. The second בית stood 420 years, which puts its destruction in the שמיטה year itself. One answer is that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who counts the fiftieth year as part of two cycles, and that recount fits. But רבי יהודה's count seems to break the first בית's timeline, which a ברייתא fixes at seventeen יובלות. The גמרא answers that the years from סנחריב's exile of the tribes until ירמיה brought them back were never counted. A second answer says the ברייתא follows the רבנן, and 'וכן בשניה' refers only to the other details of the destruction. The גמרא supports this second answer by noting that יהויריב's priestly watch was not even in the second בית. It then brings a ברייתא showing that only four priestly families returned from בבל and were divided into twenty-four watches. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: In his second year נבוכדנצר conquered יהויקים
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the previous timeline: in נבוכדנצר's second year he went up and conquered יהויקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In his second year, he went up and conquered יהויקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its earlier timeline of נבוכדנצר's reign. In his second year he went up to ארץ ישראל and conquered יהויקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the last piece of a year-by-year count of נבוכדנצר's reign that began earlier. It fixes a point in the timeline used to date the first destruction. It adds no new argument here; it simply closes that discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: He went up (to ארץ ישראל)
Conquered
יהויקים, a king of יהודה

phrases.english: In the second year he went up and conquered Jehoiakim.
phrases.notes: "He" is נבוכדנצר, and "second year" means the second year of his reign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final line of the timeline discussion carried over from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In נבוכדנצר's second year he conquered יהויקים.

steps.title: The ברייתא says the same happened at the second destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא: just as the first בית was destroyed in מוצאי שביעית, so was the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same was true of the second בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's line "and the same for the second." This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had listed details of the first destruction, including that it happened in מוצאי שביעית. It then says the second destruction matched. The גמרא now picks up that claim so it can test whether the numbers really work.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; the same
The second (בית המקדש)

phrases.english: And likewise with the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the timeline and returns to the ברייתא's statement about the second בית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second בית המקדש was destroyed under the same conditions as the first, including מוצאי שביעית.

steps.title: The 420 years don't fit מוצאי שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The second בית stood 420 years. Counted in cycles, that makes the last year year six, so the destruction fell in the שמיטה year itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can the second destruction have been in the year after שמיטה? The second בית stood 420 years. Four hundred years are eight יובלות. Fourteen more years are two seven-year cycles. That leaves six years, so the last year was the sixth of the cycle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with simple math. Counting 420 years in fifty-year and seven-year cycles, the destruction lands in the שמיטה year, not the year after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With fifty-year יובל cycles, 400 years is exactly eight יובלות. The leftover 20 years are two full שמיטה cycles (14) plus 6 more. The last full year was year six, so the destruction came in year seven, the שמיטה itself, which contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The year right after שמיטה
Can you find such a case? (a challenge)
Now, consider (introduces a known fact)
יובל cycles (normally fifty years each)
A seven-year שמיטה cycle
Remain; are left over

phrases.english: And the second, in the year after the Sabbatical Year —
can you find it?
Now, how many years did the Second Temple stand?
Four hundred and twenty.
Four hundred are eight Jubilees,
fourteen are two Sabbatical cycles,
six remain,
so it was in the sixth year of the cycle.
phrases.notes: The last year the בית stood was year six, so the destruction fell in year seven, the שמיטה itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנִיָּה בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ברייתא's claim from step 2 against the known length of the second בית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the second בית was destroyed in מוצאי שביעית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 420 years in fifty-year יובל cycles leaves the last year as year six, so the destruction falls in the שמיטה year, not the year after.
steps.confusionAlert: This count assumes every יובל cycle is a full fifty years. The answer will change exactly that assumption.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds that the fiftieth year counts both as יובל and as year one of the next cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה's, who says the fiftieth year counts for both here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. He holds that the fiftieth year (יובל) also counts as the first year of the next cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the יובל year is shared between two cycles, so each יובל cycle is really only 49 years. That changes the math from the challenge. The גמרא now has a tool to recount the years.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
The fiftieth year, the יובל
Counts for both sides: as יובל and as year one of the next cycle

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a disagreement about counting יובל years can decide historical dating questions.

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda's,
who said: "The fiftieth year
counts for here and for there,"
phrases.notes: Literally "goes up to here and to here." The fiftieth year is both the יובל and year one of the new cycle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא whose counting method changes the calculation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each יובל cycle is a full fifty years, so the destruction fell in the שמיטה year.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה each cycle is 49 years, which shifts the count.

steps.title: The recount lands in מוצאי שביעית
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יהודה, eight extra years come from the eight יובלות. Added to the six, they make fourteen, so the destruction falls in מוצאי שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring eight years from the eight יובלות. Together with those six, that makes fourteen. So it turns out the בית was destroyed in the year after שמיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא redoes the math using רבי יהודה's count. Now the destruction lands exactly in מוצאי שביעית, just as the ברייתא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the eight יובל cycles is one year shorter, which frees up eight years for the seven-year count. Eight plus the six leftover years makes fourteen, which is two full שמיטה cycles. So the 420th year ends a cycle, and the destruction falls in year one of the next cycle, the year after שמיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring; add in
It turns out
It was destroyed

steps.whatToRemember: By plain fifty-year cycles, the second בית fell in a שמיטה year. By רבי יהודה's 49-year cycles, it fell in מוצאי שביעית, matching the ברייתא.

phrases.english: bring eight from the eight Jubilees,
phrases.notes: One extra year from each of the eight יובל cycles, since each cycle is now 49 years.

phrases.english: and these six make fourteen,
it turns out that it was destroyed in the year after the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יהודה's rule from step 4 to redo the calculation from step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יהודה, the second בית המקדש was destroyed in מוצאי שביעית. The next step tests whether this also works for the first בית.

steps.title: The רבי יהודה answer fails for the first בית
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, the first בית could not have been destroyed in מוצאי שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, then for the first בית you cannot make it work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. This short line opens the challenge, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said both בתים were destroyed in מוצאי שביעית. Using רבי יהודה fixed the count for the second בית. The גמרא now says this same approach ruins the count for the first בית.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot find it, meaning the claim cannot work out
In the first one, here meaning the first בית

phrases.english: If it follows רבי יהודה,
then for the first [בית] you cannot find it!
phrases.notes: He means you cannot find the first destruction falling in מוצאי שביעית.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from steps 4-5 by testing it on the first בית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An answer that fixes the second בית must not break the first בית, which the same ברייתא also discusses.

steps.title: A ברייתא counts seventeen יובלות in the first בית period
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says Israel counted seventeen יובלות from entering the land until the exile, starting the count only after fourteen years of conquest and division.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Israel counted seventeen יובלות from when they entered the land until they left. You cannot say they started counting the moment they entered, because then the בית would have been destroyed at the start of a יובל cycle, and you would not find the פסוק 'in the fourteenth year after the city was struck'. Rather, take away the seven years of conquest and the seven years of dividing the land, and then you find 'in the fourteenth year after the city was struck.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the exact timeline of the first בית. This is the data it will use to show that רבי יהודה's count does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא fixes two facts: seventeen יובלות were counted, and the counting began only after fourteen years of conquest and division. That start point makes a יובל year fall fourteen years after the destruction, matching the פסוק in יחזקאל. This ברייתא counts יובלות as full fifty-year cycles.

keyTerms.meaning: Jubilee cycles of fifty years
That they conquered, the seven years of conquering the land
That they divided, the seven years of dividing the land among the tribes
The city was struck, meaning ירושלים was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: The fourteen years appear twice in different roles: fourteen years of conquest and division before counting began, and the פסוק's 'fourteenth year' after the destruction. The ברייתא uses the first to explain the second.

phrases.english: As it is taught: seventeen יובלות
Israel counted from when they entered the land
until they left,
and you cannot say
that they counted from the moment they entered,
because if you say so —
it turns out the בית was destroyed at the start of a יובל cycle,
and you would not find

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״.
phrases.english: "in the fourteenth year after the city was struck."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 40:1. The ברייתא reads this פסוק as describing a יובל year.

phrases.english: Rather, take away from them the seven years that they conquered,
and the seven years that they divided [the land],
and then you find

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״.
phrases.english: "in the fourteenth year after the city was struck."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹבֵלוֹת מָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the first בית could not have been destroyed in מוצאי שביעית under רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא counting seventeen יובלות from fourteen years after the entry into the land until the exile.

steps.title: Under רבי יהודה the first destruction lands in year three
steps.stepSummary: If each of the seventeen יובלות gives an extra year, the first destruction would fall in the third year of the seven-year cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it follows רבי יהודה, take seventeen extra years from the seventeen יובלות and add them on. Then the destruction would be in the third year of the seven-year cycle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by doing the math. Under רבי יהודה the first destruction lands in the wrong year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the fiftieth year also counts as year one of the next cycle, so each יובל shifts the seven-year count by one year. Seventeen יובלות means seventeen shifted years. Those extra years push the first destruction into the third year of the cycle instead of מוצאי שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: Seventeen (Aramaic)
Throw them onto these, meaning add them to the count
Here, a seven-year שמיטה cycle

phrases.english: And if it follows רבי יהודה,
bring seventeen [years] from the seventeen יובלות,
phrases.notes: One extra year from each יובל, because רבי יהודה counts the fiftieth year twice.

phrases.english: add them onto these —
it comes out in the third year of the seven-year cycle!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אַיְיתִי שַׁבְסְרֵי מִשַּׁבְסְרֵי יוֹבֵלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יהודה's counting method to the data from the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא about both destructions follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seventeen יובלות under רבי יהודה add seventeen shifted years, which puts the first destruction in year three, not מוצאי שביעית.

steps.title: The years of the ten tribes' exile were not counted
steps.stepSummary: From סנחריב's exile of the tribes until ירמיה brought them back, the יובל count stopped, so not all seventeen extra years apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those years when סנחריב exiled them, until ירמיה came and brought them back, were not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says there was a gap when the יובל count stopped, so the math in step 8 does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the יובל count ran without a break through the whole first בית period. The answer says that from סנחריב's exile of the tribes until ירמיה returned them, the years were not counted at all. After the return a fresh count began, and the destruction came 36 years later, which is the year right after a שמיטה, even by רבי יהודה's count.

keyTerms.meaning: He exiled them
He brought them back
He does not count them, meaning those years are left out of the count

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה for both בתים, because the years between סנחריב's exile and ירמיה's return were left out of the יובל count.

phrases.english: Those years when סנחריב exiled them,
until ירמיה came and brought them back —
he does not count them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the calculation challenge of step 8 by changing which years are counted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the count: a stretch of years is removed from the יובל calculation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יובל count ran without a break, so all seventeen extra years must be added.
steps.terutzMaskana: The years from סנחריב's exile until ירמיה's return were not counted, so the destruction still fits מוצאי שביעית under רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Second answer: the ברייתא follows the רבנן and 'likewise' covers only the other details
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can follow the רבנן, because 'וכן בשניה' refers only to the other details of the destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: the ברייתא really follows the רבנן. When it says 'and the same happened in the second,' it means the other details, not all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question about the ברייתא. It says the ברייתא can follow the רבנן, and 'וכן בשניה' does not copy every detail onto the second בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא assumed 'וכן בשניה' means everything about the first destruction also happened in the second, including the timing in the שמיטה cycle. This answer narrows those words to only the remaining details. That way the year count of the רבנן no longer causes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces a second, alternative answer
Actually / really: we keep the original position after all
The Sages, who disagree with רבי יהודה about counting the יובל year
And likewise in the second: the ברייתא's words comparing the second destruction to the first
To the rest: to the other details only

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, it follows the Rabbis,
and when it teaches 'and likewise in the second,'
it refers to the rest.
phrases.notes: 'The rest' means the other details in the ברייתא, like the date and day of the week, not the year in the שמיטה cycle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge in step 3, replacing the רבי יהודה answer of steps 4-5 (and so making the challenge and answer of steps 6-9 unnecessary).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וכן בשניה' applies every detail, including the year in the שמיטה cycle, to the second destruction, which forced the ברייתא to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וכן בשניה' applies only to the other details, so the ברייתא can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: Support: the watch of יהויריב could not have served in the second בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the limited reading: otherwise the ברייתא would claim that יהויריב's watch served when the second בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This makes sense. If you don't say so, was יהויריב's priestly watch even there in the second בית המקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second answer is logical. The ברייתא's details cannot all apply to the second destruction, because one of them is about יהויריב's watch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the first destruction happened during the week of יהויריב's watch. If 'וכן בשניה' covered everything, the same would have to be true of the second destruction. The גמרא suggests that this watch did not exist in the second בית המקדש period, and it is about to bring proof.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable: a logical support for what was just said
For if you do not say so: introduces the problem that the other reading would cause
Priestly watch: one of the 24 groups of כהנים that took turns serving in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if you do not say so,
the priestly watch of Jehoiarib,
was it there in the second Temple?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 10 with logic
steps.raayaObject: That 'וכן בשניה' does not apply every detail to the second destruction
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's mention of יהויריב's watch, which seemingly did not exist in the second בית המקדש period

steps.title: ברייתא: only four watches came back from בבל and were split into twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that only four priestly families returned from exile, and the prophets divided them into twenty-four watches by lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: four watches came up from exile: ידעיה, חרים, פשחור, and אמר. The prophets among them divided them into twenty-four watches. They mixed up the lots and put them in a box. ידעיה came and drew his own lot and lots for his fellow watches: six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove that יהויריב's original watch did not return from בבל. Only four families came back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only four families returned, the original יהויריב family was not among the כהנים of the second בית המקדש. The prophets rebuilt twenty-four watches by having each returning family draw lots for six watches. ידעיה drew first, and the ברייתא continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: The exile: here, the Jews exiled to בבל
Prophets: here, the prophets among those who returned
They mixed them up: shuffled the lots
A box or urn for drawing lots

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
four priestly watches came up from the exile:
Jedaiah, Harim, Pashhur, and Immer.
The prophets among them arose
and divided them into twenty-four watches.
They mixed them up and put them in a lottery box.
Jedaiah came and took his own portion
and the portion of his fellows: six.
phrases.notes: He drew his own lot plus five more, so ידעיה ended up with six watches in total.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אַרְבַּע מִשְׁמָרוֹת עָלוּ מִן הַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that backs up the claim in step 11
steps.raayaObject: That יהויריב's original watch was not present in the second בית המקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that only ידעיה, חרים, פשחור, and אמר returned from exile and were divided into twenty-four watches by lottery
